research.angle: While probiotics show promise in reducing depression symptoms when used alongside traditional antidepressants, they do not appear effective as a stand-alone treatment and show no effect in people over 65.
research.verdict: The evidence suggests that gut microbiota interventions, specifically probiotics, may improve mild-to-moderate depression as an adjunctive therapy but are not currently sufficient as a primary treatment.
research.caveat: Most studies indicate that further research is needed to determine the benefits of these therapies relative to antidepressants and over longer follow-up periods.
